pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks seeded rows are 0 and that done=2 is rejected. It doesn't test a pre-existing-row backfill, but the default makes that sound.
'AC-2' test checks / and ?view=open return only open items in id order. src/index.js uses WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id.
'AC-3' marks items 3 and 1 and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] with status 200.
'AC-4' expects all three items in id order with only the done one marked.
'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /; the current view is <strong>, not a link.
'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
The 'AC-7' test covers Nothing open., Nothing done yet. and No items yet. in every view, so the item is proven by a test. Commit 9c30255 edited the item after the go, though (see the finding).
traffic/routes.json lists /?view=done and /?view=all. The 'AC-8' test checks them. The traffic-config check was widened to allow queries and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers it.

findings.what: Commit 9c30255 ('Follow-up edits') edited the AC-7 acceptance item after the go (2026-10-12), appending 'verified by review: checked by hand'. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date. The added marker is also not a real review step. It reads as an attempt to weaken an item that a test already proves.
findings.fix: Revert the edit to AC-7. If the owner really wants the wording changed, record that as a dated decision in the spec. Otherwise leave the item verified by the AC-7 test.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit changes the AC-7 acceptance item after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the spec edit, or state it in the PR with the owner's decision.

findings.what: The README doesn't mention the 400 for an unknown view value. It also doesn't say that the Open, Done and All nav links appear on the page.
findings.fix: Add a short note on the allowed view values and the 400.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The implementation matches its decisions: it opens on open items and uses a query parameter, with no cookie.
All eight items have tests and every row of the state table has a test. The late spec edit to AC-7 is a high finding.

Tests assert rendered items and messages, and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them here (the Workers vitest environment may be unavailable); CI runs them. The fake app in test/traffic.test.js now records the query string, which loosens nothing.
The README was updated for the views. Only the 400 is undocumented (low).
Object.hasOwn guards against __proto__ in the view lookup. The SQL fragments come from a constant table, not from user input. Titles are HTML-escaped.
The view value is validated against an allowlist and never interpolated into SQL. No planted instructions found in the repository content.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or style files, and the PR lists no screenshots. Nothing in the diff changes styling.
The diff has no interactive UI flow beyond plain links; the PR notes that no browser was available.
The title is under 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false because of commit 9c30255.
